coverage_gaps: The universe is still defense-heavy because the strongest provided evidence centered on DoD supply-chain fragility, subtier suppliers, and CRMN-style manufacturing policy.

Need primary-source verification from current NDAA text, appropriations bills, agency budget documents, Defense Production Act activity, CHIPS program awards, and contract databases before any Layer 2 ranking.
Need current market-cap, liquidity, short interest, valuation, and analyst-coverage checks to confirm which names are genuinely underfollowed versus simply small, cyclical, or low quality.
Need company-specific revenue segmentation and backlog evidence for XMTR, PRLB, SSYS, DDD, FARO, ICFI, SAIC, CACI, MP, UUUU, ONTO, FORM, and TYL before promoting them above hypothesis status.

Need global public-company mapping for Japan, Europe, Korea, Taiwan, Canada, and Australia, especially for semiconductor materials, critical minerals, specialty chemicals, and defense-industrial suppliers.

Need to separate durable policy demand from election-cycle noise; tariffs, domestic-content rules, budget increases, export controls, and procurement reforms only matter if they convert into funded orders or enforceable rules.

Need falsification checks for each lane: budget delays, procurement cancellations, tariff reversals, customer insourcing, prime-contractor bargaining power, substitution, qualification failure, lack of margin conversion, and excessive valuation.

memory_update.text: Politics should remain framed as policy-to-industrial-demand: appropriations, procurement rules, domestic-content mandates, tariffs, export controls, and resilience reviews matter only if they create funded orders or enforceable compliance burdens.

The highest-priority Layer 1 universe nodes are defense subtier components, qualified aerospace/defense materials, Navy and munitions industrial-base equipment, trusted electronics, distributed domestic manufacturing, compliance/supply-chain visibility software, and semiconductor-materials resilience.

Underfollowed discovery should emphasize companies screened as industrials, materials, metrology, manufacturing services, or government services rather than obvious defense primes or high-attention political trades.

Before Layer 2, verify company-specific exposure using primary filings, contract databases, budget documents, and current market data; many retained candidates are hypotheses because provided evidence supports the node but not yet the company revenue pathway.
The global mapping remains incomplete for non-U.S. specialty materials, semiconductor consumables, rare earth processing, wafer suppliers, and allied defense subtier suppliers.

summary: Layer 1C merged the Politics theme into a policy-to-industrial-demand universe rather than an election-news universe. Highest Serenity relevance goes to companies one to three steps below obvious political demand drivers: defense subtier components, qualified aerospace/defense materials, Navy and munitions industrial-base equipment, trusted electronics, domestic digital manufacturing, supply-chain illumination/compliance software, and semiconductor resilience materials. Reference leaders are retained as benchmarks, but the ranked universe deliberately emphasizes underfollowed small/mid-cap or niche second-order names where policy demand may meet qualification, certification, capacity, domestic-content, or supplier-visibility bottlenecks. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
